resolutions.researcher_notes: Replaces the DEAD_LINK aramco.com original. StartYear1=2028 supported: the Master Gas System phase-three expansion is to add 3.15 bscfd capacity (~4,000 km of pipeline, 17 compression trains) 'by 2028', with completion scheduled for Q4 2028. SPA (official Saudi Press Agency, N2131194, 30 Jun 2024 award announcement) and World Oil both carry '2028' and 'Master Gas System'. Caveat: both trace to Aramco's 30 Jun 2024 award announcement, but SPA is the state wire and World Oil is independent trade press; corroborated further by MEED and BlackRidge project profiles (not cited). No contradiction to the 2028 value.

StartCountryOrArea=EndCountryOrArea=Saudi Arabia supported: the Master Gas System is Aramco's domestic Saudi network that 'delivers natural gas to customers across the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia'; the MGS III expansion pipelines are entirely within Saudi Arabia. Both SPA and World Oil carry 'Saudi'/'Kingdom of Saudi Arabia' plus 'Master Gas System'. No cross-border element in this segment; consistent with EWPS-6 to EWPS-8 being internal MGS nodes.

Replaces DEAD_LINK aramco.com + unverifiable meed.com originals. Owner1=Aramco 100% supported: the Master Gas System is owned/operated by Saudi Aramco, which awarded the phase-three (MGS-3) EPC packages as project owner. SPA (official, 30 Jun 2024) confirms Aramco owns the MGS expansion; OGJ independently reports Aramco awarding the $1.4bn MGS-3 pipeline package to a Sinopec unit — a separate contract-award story confirming Aramco as principal/owner. Both carry 'Aramco' and 'Master Gas System'. No indication of any co-owner; 100% Aramco is consistent with all sources.
